goal: Build h2 to satisfy the complete public pure-Python HTTP/2 protocol library specification.

atoms.title: Sans-I/O pure-Python HTTP/2 library
atoms.input: After offline installation, import h2.connection, h2.config, h2.events, h2.errors, h2.settings and h2.exceptions with socket creation blocked, and drive a client/server H2Connection pair only by passing data_to_send() bytes into the other side's receive_data().
atoms.expected: All modules import as pure Python and the pair exchanges binary HTTP/2 frames (decodable by hyperframe) carrying HPACK-compressed headers, multiplexed streams, flow-control and SETTINGS frames, without the library opening a socket or performing I/O.

atoms.title: Caller-driven bytes-in/bytes-out model
atoms.input: Call a send method (ping, send_headers) on a connection, call data_to_send(), feed the bytes into the peer's receive_data(); call data_to_send() again.
atoms.expected: The send method only queues bytes; data_to_send() returns and drains them (the next call returns b""); receive_data() returns a list of the events those bytes produced.

atoms.title: Example construction and handshake
atoms.input: Run the example import line, build client (client_side=True) and server (client_side=False) H2Connection objects via config=H2Configuration(...), then run both initiate_connection() calls and the two receive_data(data_to_send()) exchanges exactly as shown.
atoms.expected: Imports succeed, both constructors accept the config keyword, no exception is raised, each receive_data returns a list, and both connections are ready for the request step (the following send_headers succeeds).

atoms.title: Example GET delivered as RequestReceived
atoms.input: After the example handshake: client.send_headers(1, [(":method","GET"), (":path","/"), (":scheme","https"), (":authority","example.com")], end_stream=True); server.receive_data(client.data_to_send()).
atoms.expected: The returned list contains a RequestReceived for stream 1 whose headers carry the four request headers (bytes tuples under the default header_encoding) and, later in the list, a StreamEnded for stream 1. Other events and their positions are unspecified.
gaps: The request comment "[RequestReceived, StreamEnded, ...]" permits further events; which ones and where is unspecified.

atoms.title: Example response delivered as ResponseReceived, DataReceived, StreamEnded
atoms.input: Continue the example: server.send_headers(1, [(":status","200")]); server.send_data(1, b"hello", end_stream=True); client.receive_data(server.data_to_send()).
atoms.expected: The returned list contains ResponseReceived (stream 1, headers including (b":status", b"200")), DataReceived (stream 1, data b"hello") and StreamEnded (stream 1), in that order.
gaps: The response comment lists exactly three events; whether any other event may also appear in that list is unspecified.

atoms.title: Offline: nothing installed, downloaded or fetched
atoms.input: Run setup.sh and every library operation in a container with network disabled, PIP_NO_INDEX=1 and only the pre-installed packages.
atoms.expected: Installation and library use succeed without installing, downloading or fetching anything and without any network access attempt.

atoms.title: hyperframe and hpack runtime dependencies
atoms.input: Run a client/server round trip in an environment whose only third-party packages are the pre-installed hyperframe and hpack; inspect the installed distribution's declared requirements.
atoms.expected: The library works with hyperframe (frame serialization/parsing) and hpack (header compression) and needs no other third-party runtime package; frames it emits parse with hyperframe and header blocks decode with hpack.
gaps: Whether hyperframe/hpack must be used internally and declared in packaging metadata, or merely be compatible, is unspecified.

atoms.title: Offline editable install through setup.sh
atoms.input: Copy the candidate project to a fresh environment holding the pre-installed dependencies, run its setup.sh with no network and PIP_NO_INDEX=1, then import h2.connection from an unrelated working directory.
atoms.expected: setup.sh performs `pip install -e . --no-build-isolation` successfully against the pre-installed dependencies, and h2 then imports from the editable install.
gaps: The text does not say whether the candidate must author setup.sh and the packaging file or whether they are provided.

atoms.title: H2Configuration signature and defaults
atoms.input: Construct H2Configuration() with no arguments and H2Configuration(client_side=False, header_encoding="utf-8"); use each as H2Connection(config=...) and run a request.
atoms.expected: Both keyword arguments are accepted; omitted arguments default to client_side=True and header_encoding=None, so the no-argument configuration behaves as a client whose events carry bytes headers. Whether the values are readable as attributes is unspecified.

atoms.title: client_side selects stream parity and preface
atoms.input: Create connections with client_side=True and client_side=False; call initiate_connection() and get_next_available_stream_id() on each.
atoms.expected: The client-side connection emits the connection preface magic and uses odd stream IDs; the server-side connection emits no magic and uses even stream IDs.

atoms.title: header_encoding selects bytes or str headers
atoms.input: Deliver the same request to a server configured with header_encoding=None and to one configured with header_encoding="utf-8".
atoms.expected: With None (the default) RequestReceived.headers holds bytes tuples such as (b":method", b"GET"); with "utf-8" it holds str tuples such as (":method", "GET").

atoms.title: H2Connection constructor and external I/O
atoms.input: Construct H2Connection() with config omitted and H2Connection(config=H2Configuration(...)) with socket creation blocked.
atoms.expected: Both constructions succeed; the object processes byte buffers only and never performs network I/O. Which role and header encoding apply when config is None is unspecified.
gaps: The configuration implied by H2Connection(config=None) is not stated.

atoms.title: initiate_connection preface per role
atoms.input: Call initiate_connection() on a fresh client and on a fresh server connection; decode each data_to_send() with hyperframe.
atoms.expected:
Client output starts with the 24 bytes b"PRI * HTTP/2.0

SM

" immediately followed by a non-ACK SETTINGS frame on stream 0; server output starts with a SETTINGS frame and contains no magic.

atoms.title: Client HTTP/1.1 upgrade
atoms.input: On a fresh client call initiate_upgrade_connection() without settings_header; base64url-decode the result (padding-tolerant); inspect data_to_send(); query stream 1.
atoms.expected: The return value is bytes that base64url-decode to a SETTINGS payload of 6-byte identifier/value entries describing the client settings; the connection preface is queued; stream 1 exists (local_flow_control_window(1) returns an int instead of raising NoSuchStreamError).

atoms.title: Server HTTP/1.1 upgrade
atoms.input: Pass a client's upgrade value (and separately a hand-built base64url SETTINGS payload, e.g. MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS=10) to a fresh server's initiate_upgrade_connection(settings_header=...); then server.send_headers(1, [(":status","200")]).
atoms.expected: The call accepts the header and adopts those values as the client's settings; stream 1 is open so the response headers are sent on stream 1 without the server opening a new stream.
gaps: Whether the server upgrade call queues the server's own SETTINGS or returns a value is unspecified.

atoms.title: receive_data returns events and queues automatic responses
atoms.input: Feed a peer SETTINGS frame and a non-ACK PING frame with 8 opaque bytes into receive_data(); decode data_to_send().
atoms.expected: receive_data returns a list of event objects; the outbound buffer then holds a SETTINGS frame with the ACK flag and a PING frame with the ACK flag carrying the same 8 bytes.

atoms.title: Handshake RemoteSettingsChanged enumerates advertised settings
atoms.input: Feed a fresh server the client magic plus a hyperframe SETTINGS frame advertising HEADER_TABLE_SIZE=4096, INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE=65535, MAX_FRAME_SIZE=16384, MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS=100 (all equal to the documented defaults); repeat with differing values (e.g. MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS=50, INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE=1000); repeat client-side with a server SETTINGS.
atoms.expected: The returned list includes a RemoteSettingsChanged whose changed_settings has a SettingCodes-keyed entry for every advertised setting, including values equal to the defaults; each ChangedSetting.original_value equals the receiver's documented default (4096, 65535, 16384, 100) and new_value the advertised value.
gaps: original_value for advertised settings without a documented default (ENABLE_PUSH, MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE) is unspecified.

atoms.title: data_to_send returns and drains pending output
atoms.input: Call data_to_send() on a fresh connection; call initiate_connection(); call data_to_send() twice.
atoms.expected: The fresh call returns b""; the first call after initiate_connection returns all queued bytes as bytes; the immediately following call returns b"".

atoms.title: clear_outbound_data_buffer discards output
atoms.input: Call initiate_connection() (or ping), then clear_outbound_data_buffer(), then data_to_send(); then ping again and call data_to_send().
atoms.expected: The first data_to_send() returns b"" and the discarded bytes never appear; the later ping is queued and returned normally.

atoms.title: send_headers emits HEADERS and opens the stream
atoms.input: After a handshake, client.send_headers(1, request_headers) with end_stream False, and on another pair with end_stream=True; decode with hyperframe and hpack; then call send_data on the end_stream=True stream.
atoms.expected: Exactly one HEADERS frame on stream 1 whose header block decodes to the given (name, value) strings; END_STREAM is set only when end_stream=True; the stream counts as open; after end_stream=True a send_data on it raises ProtocolError.

atoms.title: Client stream ID rules and closed-stream send_headers
atoms.input: On a handshaken client: send_headers on even stream 2; open stream 5 then send_headers on stream 3; send_headers on stream 1 after it was reset or closed on both sides.
atoms.expected: Each call raises an instance of h2.exceptions.ProtocolError.

atoms.title: TooManyStreamsError beyond MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS
atoms.input: The server advertises MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS=1 with update_settings and the client receives it; the client opens stream 1 without ending it, then calls send_headers on stream 3.
atoms.expected: The second send_headers raises TooManyStreamsError.
gaps: Which MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS (peer-advertised or the local default 100) bounds send_headers is not stated; the case uses the peer-advertised value.

atoms.title: send_data emits exactly one DATA frame
atoms.input: On an open stream call send_data(1, b"hello") and send_data(1, b"x" * 16384, end_stream=True); decode output and deliver it to the peer.
atoms.expected: Each call emits exactly one DATA frame on that stream carrying the given bytes; END_STREAM only on the end_stream=True call; the peer receives DataReceived with matching data then StreamEnded.

atoms.title: send_data FlowControlError beyond the window
atoms.input: With default 65535 windows, open a stream and send three 16384-byte frames (leaving 16383 bytes), then send_data with 16384 bytes (within MAX_FRAME_SIZE).
atoms.expected: The fourth call raises FlowControlError.

atoms.title: send_data FrameTooLargeError beyond MAX_FRAME_SIZE
atoms.input: On a fresh open stream with default settings (MAX_FRAME_SIZE 16384, windows 65535) call send_data with 16385 bytes.
atoms.expected: FrameTooLargeError is raised; the data is never split across several frames.

atoms.title: Flow-control check precedes frame-size check
atoms.input: On a fresh open stream with default settings call send_data with 65536 bytes (over both the 65535 window and 16384 MAX_FRAME_SIZE); on another stream whose window is exhausted call send_data with 16385 bytes.
atoms.expected: Both calls raise FlowControlError, not FrameTooLargeError.

atoms.title: send_data after the send side closed
atoms.input: Close stream 1's send side by send_headers(..., end_stream=True) and, separately, by end_stream(1); call send_data(1, b"x").
atoms.expected: An instance of ProtocolError is raised in both cases.

atoms.title: end_stream sends an empty END_STREAM DATA frame
atoms.input: Open stream 1 with send_headers (end_stream False), call end_stream(1), decode data_to_send(), deliver it to the peer, then call send_data(1, b"x").
atoms.expected: One DATA frame with an empty payload and END_STREAM on stream 1 is queued; the peer receives StreamEnded for stream 1; the subsequent send_data raises ProtocolError.

atoms.title: Next available stream ID parity and increment
atoms.input: On a handshaken client repeatedly call get_next_available_stream_id() and open the returned stream; on a handshaken server with a client request on stream 1, get an ID and push_stream with it, twice.
atoms.expected: The client gets 1, 3, 5 as each returned ID is opened; the server gets 2 then 4.
gaps: Whether repeated calls without opening a stream return the same ID is unspecified.

atoms.title: reset_stream emits RST_STREAM
atoms.input: Open streams 1 and 3; call reset_stream(1) and reset_stream(3, error_code=ErrorCodes.CANCEL); decode output and feed it to the peer.
atoms.expected: One RST_STREAM frame per stream with error code 0 (default) and 8 (CANCEL); the peer receives StreamReset events with matching stream_id and error_code.
gaps: reset_stream refers to "§6" for ErrorCodes, which the text defines in §4.

atoms.title: push_stream emits PUSH_PROMISE
atoms.input: Client sends a request on stream 1; server calls push_stream(1, server.get_next_available_stream_id(), [(":method","GET"), (":path","/style.css"), (":scheme","https"), (":authority","example.com")]); deliver to the client.
atoms.expected: A PUSH_PROMISE frame on stream 1 promising even stream 2 with those headers; the client receives PushedStreamReceived with parent_stream_id 1, pushed_stream_id 2 and the promised headers.

atoms.title: push_stream refused after the peer disables push
atoms.input: Client calls update_settings({SettingCodes.ENABLE_PUSH: 0}) and the server receives it; client sends a request on stream 1; server calls push_stream(1, 2, headers).
atoms.expected: push_stream raises ProtocolError and no PUSH_PROMISE frame is emitted.

atoms.title: close_connection emits GOAWAY
atoms.input: Call close_connection() on one pair and close_connection(error_code=ErrorCodes.PROTOCOL_ERROR, last_stream_id=5) on another; decode output and feed it to the peer.
atoms.expected: A GOAWAY frame with error code 0 by default and 1 / last stream id 5 in the explicit case; the peer receives ConnectionTerminated with matching error_code and last_stream_id.
gaps: The last_stream_id emitted when close_connection(last_stream_id=None) is unspecified.

atoms.title: Received GOAWAY rejects new streams
atoms.input: Server calls close_connection(); the client receives it and then calls send_headers on a new stream ID.
atoms.expected: The client refuses to open the new stream by raising an h2.exceptions error.
gaps: How "rejects new streams" surfaces (exception type) is unspecified.

atoms.title: prioritize emits PRIORITY; peer gets PriorityUpdated
atoms.input: Open streams 1 and 3; call prioritize(3, weight=32, depends_on=1, exclusive=True) and prioritize(1); decode and feed to the peer.
atoms.expected: PRIORITY frames for streams 3 and 1; the peer receives PriorityUpdated with (stream 3, weight 32, depends_on 1, exclusive True) and (stream 1, weight 16, depends_on 0). The default exclusive value and out-of-range weights are unspecified.

atoms.title: local_flow_control_window tracks sendable bytes
atoms.input: After a default handshake, open stream 1, read local_flow_control_window(1), send_data 1000 bytes, read it again.
gaps: Whether the value is the stream window alone or the minimum of stream and connection windows is unspecified.

atoms.title: local_flow_control_window on an unknown stream
atoms.input: On a handshaken connection call local_flow_control_window(7) for a stream never opened.
atoms.expected: NoSuchStreamError is raised.

atoms.title: remote_flow_control_window reports the peer's window
atoms.input: Client opens stream 1 and reads remote_flow_control_window(1); the server sends 1000 bytes of DATA on stream 1; the client receives it without acknowledging and reads again.
atoms.expected: Initially 65535 (the client's default INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE); after the 1000 unacknowledged bytes, 64535.

atoms.title: acknowledge_received_data allows WINDOW_UPDATE
atoms.input: Server sends three 16384-byte DATA frames on stream 1; the client calls acknowledge_received_data(event.flow_controlled_length, 1) for each DataReceived, then data_to_send() and feeds the server.
atoms.expected: Acknowledgement raises nothing; any WINDOW_UPDATE frames queued target stream 1 or the connection with increments totalling at most the acknowledged bytes, and the server's sending window grows by them.
gaps: When (threshold) and with what increment WINDOW_UPDATE is emitted after acknowledgement is unspecified.

atoms.title: increment_flow_control_window emits WINDOW_UPDATE
atoms.input: Client opens stream 1; calls increment_flow_control_window(1000) and increment_flow_control_window(500, stream_id=1); decode output and feed it to the server.
atoms.expected: A WINDOW_UPDATE on stream 0 with increment 1000 and one on stream 1 with increment 500; the server receives WindowUpdated events with delta 1000 (connection) and delta 500 (stream_id 1). The stream_id value of the connection-level event is unspecified.

atoms.title: update_settings sends SETTINGS; peer gets RemoteSettingsChanged
atoms.input: After a handshake, client.update_settings({SettingCodes.MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS: 50}); decode output; feed it to the server.
atoms.expected: A non-ACK SETTINGS frame containing MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS=50; the server receives RemoteSettingsChanged with changed_settings[SettingCodes.MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS].new_value == 50.

atoms.title: ping and automatic PING ACK
atoms.input: Client ping(b"12345678"); feed to the server; feed the server's output back to the client.
atoms.expected: A PING frame carrying the 8 bytes; the server returns PingReceived(ping_data=b"12345678") and automatically queues a PING ACK with the same data; the client receives PingAckReceived(ping_data=b"12345678"). Behaviour for non-8-byte data is unspecified.

atoms.title: advertise_alternative_service emits ALTSVC
atoms.input: After a handshake and a client request on stream 1, the server calls advertise_alternative_service(b'h2=":8000"') and advertise_alternative_service(b'h2=":8000"', stream_id=1); feed to the client.
atoms.expected: ALTSVC frames on stream 0 and on stream 1 carrying the field value; the client receives AlternativeServiceAvailable events with field_value b'h2=":8000"'.
gaps: No origin parameter exists, so the origin of a connection-level ALTSVC frame and the event's origin value are unspecified, as is which side may send ALTSVC.

atoms.title: open_outbound_streams and open_inbound_streams
atoms.input: Client opens streams 1 and 3; server receives them; client ends stream 1 (server not yet ended), then the server ends 1; client resets 3.
atoms.expected: client.open_outbound_streams and server.open_inbound_streams rise to 2, keep counting the half-closed stream 1, and drop as stream 1 closes on both sides and stream 3 is reset; client.open_inbound_streams and server.open_outbound_streams stay 0.

atoms.title: inbound_flow_control_window
atoms.input: Read inbound_flow_control_window on a fresh handshaken connection; receive 1000 bytes of DATA without acknowledging; read again.
atoms.expected: 65535 initially; 64535 after the unacknowledged 1000 bytes.

atoms.title: Event classes and attributes
atoms.input: Drive scenarios producing every listed event (request, response, data, end, reset, trailers via a second send_headers with end_stream=True, settings change/ack, window update, ping/ack, push, GOAWAY, priority, ALTSVC) and inspect each returned object.
atoms.expected: Each event is an instance of the named h2.events class and exposes the listed attributes with values from the triggering frame (stream_id where applicable; DataReceived.data is bytes with flow_controlled_length >= len(data); ConnectionTerminated has error_code, last_stream_id, additional_data). Order across frames follows the wire; extra attributes are allowed.
gaps: Types and semantics of stream_ended, priority_updated and remote_reset beyond their names are unspecified.

atoms.title: Event header value types
atoms.input: Inspect headers on RequestReceived, ResponseReceived, TrailersReceived and PushedStreamReceived under header_encoding None and "utf-8".
atoms.expected: headers is a list of (name, value) 2-tuples of bytes under None and of str under "utf-8".

atoms.title: ErrorCodes integer constants
atoms.input: Import h2.errors.ErrorCodes, read every listed member, compare with integers, and pass ErrorCodes.CANCEL to reset_stream.
atoms.expected: NO_ERROR 0, PROTOCOL_ERROR 1, INTERNAL_ERROR 2, FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR 3, SETTINGS_TIMEOUT 4, STREAM_CLOSED 5, FRAME_SIZE_ERROR 6, REFUSED_STREAM 7, CANCEL 8, COMPRESSION_ERROR 9, ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM 11; each compares equal to its integer. Codes absent from the table are unspecified.

atoms.title: SettingCodes integer constants
atoms.input: Import h2.settings.SettingCodes, read every listed member, compare with integers, and use members as keys in update_settings and changed_settings.
atoms.expected: HEADER_TABLE_SIZE 1, ENABLE_PUSH 2, MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS 3, INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE 4, MAX_FRAME_SIZE 5, MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE 6; each compares equal to its integer and works as a dict key.

atoms.title: Local setting defaults
atoms.input: Decode the SETTINGS frame a fresh connection emits from initiate_connection, and feed a fresh connection a peer SETTINGS advertising HEADER_TABLE_SIZE, INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE, MAX_FRAME_SIZE and MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS.
atoms.expected: Local settings start at HEADER_TABLE_SIZE 4096, INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE 65535, MAX_FRAME_SIZE 16384 and MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS 100 (not unlimited): any of these the initial SETTINGS frame advertises carries that value, and the handshake RemoteSettingsChanged original_value for each equals it.
gaps: Whether the initial SETTINGS frame must explicitly advertise MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS=100 ("the baseline a peer sees") is unspecified.

atoms.title: Local default does not constrain peer settings
atoms.input: A peer advertises MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS=200 (above the local default 100) in its SETTINGS; the receiver processes it.
atoms.expected: The value is accepted without error and RemoteSettingsChanged reports new_value 200; the remote setting is what the peer advertised, not capped by the local default.

atoms.title: Exception classes in h2.exceptions
atoms.input: Import ProtocolError, TooManyStreamsError, FlowControlError, FrameTooLargeError, NoSuchStreamError and StreamClosedError from h2.exceptions and trigger the documented conditions.
atoms.expected: All six exist as Exception subclasses; exceeding MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS raises TooManyStreamsError, exceeding a window FlowControlError, an oversize DATA payload FrameTooLargeError, an unknown stream NoSuchStreamError, and protocol violations ProtocolError.
gaps: Inheritance among the six exceptions, and when StreamClosedError rather than ProtocolError is raised for closed streams, is unspecified.

integration.scenario: Run the Usage example end to end under both header encodings.
integration.input: Execute the Usage code verbatim against the installed package, once with default configurations and once with header_encoding="utf-8" on both sides, decoding every data_to_send() buffer with hyperframe and hpack.
integration.expected: The handshake completes; the server sees RequestReceived and StreamEnded for stream 1 with the four request headers; the client sees ResponseReceived (:status 200), DataReceived(b"hello") and StreamEnded in order; header tuples are bytes by default and str under "utf-8"; every emitted buffer parses as HTTP/2 frames after the client magic.

integration.scenario: Negotiate settings from preface to enforcement.
integration.input: Feed a server a client preface whose hyperframe SETTINGS advertises the documented defaults; the server calls update_settings({SettingCodes.MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS: 1}), the client receives it and returns its queued bytes; the client opens one stream and attempts a second; separately a peer advertises MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS=200.
integration.expected: The handshake RemoteSettingsChanged lists every advertised setting with original_value = documented default and new_value = advertised; the client acknowledges automatically and the server receives SettingsAcknowledged; the client raises TooManyStreamsError on the second concurrent stream; the 200 advertisement is reported as advertised.

integration.scenario: Exhaust a stream window, observe the error, then recover through WINDOW_UPDATE.
integration.input: The server sends 16384-byte DATA frames on the client's stream 1 until local_flow_control_window(1) is below 16384, then attempts another 16384-byte send; the client calls increment_flow_control_window(65535) and increment_flow_control_window(65535, stream_id=1); bytes are exchanged and the server retries.
integration.expected: The over-window send raises FlowControlError; the client's inbound_flow_control_window and remote_flow_control_window(1) fall by the received bytes; the server receives WindowUpdated events, its local_flow_control_window(1) increases, and the retried send succeeds and arrives as DataReceived.

integration.scenario: End, reset and shut down streams and the connection.
integration.input: Client opens streams 1, 3 and 5; ends 1 with end_stream(1) and the server answers with end_stream=True; client resets 3 with ErrorCodes.CANCEL; server calls close_connection(ErrorCodes.NO_ERROR, last_stream_id=5) and the client receives it; the client then calls send_data(1, b"x") and send_headers on stream 7.
integration.expected: The server sees StreamEnded(1) and StreamReset(3, error_code 8); open stream counters drop as streams close or reset; the client receives ConnectionTerminated(error_code 0, last_stream_id 5); send_data on closed stream 1 raises ProtocolError and opening stream 7 is rejected.

integration.scenario: Exchange ping, push, priority and ALTSVC on one connection pair.
integration.input: On one handshaken pair with a client request on stream 1: client ping(b"abcdefgh"); server push_stream(1, 2, headers); client prioritize(1, weight=64); server advertise_alternative_service(b'h2=":8000"'). On a second pair the client disables push before the server tries push_stream.
integration.expected: PingReceived on the server and PingAckReceived on the client with the same 8 bytes; PushedStreamReceived(parent 1, pushed 2); PriorityUpdated(stream 1, weight 64) on the server; AlternativeServiceAvailable with the field value on the client; on the second pair push_stream raises ProtocolError.

integration.scenario: Complete an HTTP/1.1 upgrade and answer the upgraded request on stream 1.
integration.input: client.initiate_upgrade_connection() yields the HTTP2-Settings value; server.initiate_upgrade_connection(settings_header=value); the server sends send_headers(1, [(":status","200")]) and send_data(1, b"ok", end_stream=True); both sides exchange queued bytes (client first); the client then asks for its next stream ID.
integration.expected: The client receives ResponseReceived, DataReceived(b"ok") and StreamEnded on stream 1 without having opened stream 1 with send_headers; the client's next available stream ID is 3.
